ChatOpenItem.description: An inline item that waits on the human: which message, and what it asks for.

for.description: The person it waits on (its message's `for`); absent: anyone.

ChatOpenItemKind.description: `ChatItem`'s kind, or `memory_hold`: a bot memory line held for an admin's OK, one per owner or admin.

ChatOpenNudge.description: A nudge still waiting, in a chat state: its message, and what to look at.

ChatStatusLine.description: A bot's status line, as its lead last wrote it (`checklist`'s `status`): where things stand, in one short line.

ProjectChatState.description: One chat's state, for the sidebar and the status row.

lastSeq.description: The newest message's `seq`; 0 for an empty chat.

leadAsleep.description:
The lead's computer is asleep (fleetd cloud): the next message starts it before the lead reads it. Absent: awake,
or a hub whose leads never sleep.

leadIdleAt.description:
When the lead's latest turn ended, while it isn't mid-turn, on the hub's clock; the epoch when none is kept (no turn
yet, or one past the event log's retention). A person's message from before it was in the chat when a turn ended,
answered or not (a quiet turn). Absent: mid-turn, or an older hub.

needsYou.description: The lead's last message waits for a human reply, or an inline item is open.

needsYouFor.description:
Who what waits is for, when `needsYou`: each open item's and each unanswered question's person. Absent: it waits on
everyone (something with no `for`, or an older hub).

nudges.description: The nudges still waiting to be seen, oldest first: what the app shows as "N to look at". Absent when none is.

openItems.description:
The inline items still open, oldest first, however far back: the chat may not have their page loaded. Absent
when none is (and from older hubs).

status.description:
Where things stand, in the lead's own short line (`checklist`'s `status`): what the sidebar and the phone's chat list show
under the bot's name. Absent: none written, a person wrote since, or an older hub.

ProjectRef.description:
A project: a workspace with a lead and its own directory, on its home machine, where the lead runs. Its
`projectId` is the node's id for that directory, so the ref also addresses the files; the directory may be a git
repo or a plain folder. A project holds zero or more repos (`ProjectRepo`), each in a node directory of its
own or in the project's.
